root_idea.summary: The root has two distinct lexical axes: a plant axis represented by حُرْضٌ, the alkali plant, and إِحْرِيضٌ, safflower; and an axis of wasting, deterioration, weakness, and approaching destruction.
root_idea.development: The deterioration axis extends from bodily or mental disorder and wasting to near death, destruction, and related causative uses. Derived forms also include urging someone toward action, conventionally understood as removing or overcoming a state of debility. The plant vocabulary remains a separate lexical branch.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form II perfect citation form.
Displayed as the normalized nominal citation form.

senses.definition: To urge, incite, or encourage someone to undertake an action, rousing determination and making the undertaking seem manageable.
senses.usage_conditions: Takes عَلَى with the action or matter urged. In the Quranic occurrences it is an imperative urging believers to fight or persevere in fighting.

senses.definition: Extreme debility or wasting, approaching death; a condition in which a person is no longer reckoned with because illness or grief has consumed the person’s strength.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic usage, it describes the state to which Jacob is said to be brought by prolonged grief. The lexical explanation includes being heavily oppressed by disease, emaciated by grief or excessive love, and near death.

senses.definition: The alkali plant known as أُشْنَان, used for washing and for obtaining potash.
senses.usage_conditions: This is reported as the interpretation of a variant Quranic reading at Yusuf 12:85; it is distinct from the standard QAC reading and contextual sense at that location.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become physically disordered or diseased; to waste away through grief or excessive love, become heavily oppressed by illness, and approach or reach death.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form I use, said of the stomach or of a person; one form is also reported for dying or perishing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become low, base, mean, sordid, bad, corrupt, or neglected.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical Form I use with the forms and vocalizations reported in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pick up safflower, إِحْرِيض, from the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized verbal use referring to the plant name إِحْرِيض.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rid someone of حَرَض, removing a debilitating or corrupting condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative Form II use with the opposite direction from the urging sense: removal of the condition called حَرَض.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person entrusted with turning, shuffling, or dealing the gaming arrows in the game of maysir; by extension, a low or mean person who eats meat only when it is provided by others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is associated with the person who deals the arrows without contributing to the slaughtered animal and with the corresponding social judgment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To employ designated property in trade involving حُرْض, the alkali plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form II commercial use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dye a garment or piece of cloth with safflower, إِحْرِيض.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form II use referring to safflower dye.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To contend with another in shuffling or playing with gaming arrows.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III reciprocal use connected with the gaming-arrow vocabulary.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To apply oneself constantly or perseveringly to work or to fighting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III construction with عَلَى and the activity pursued.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to become sick, disordered, or near death; disease, food, or love may be the causing force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative Form IV use applied to disease, food that makes one ill, or love that disorders a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To corrupt, vitiate, mar, destroy, annul, or render something void; also, to destroy oneself or one’s own soul.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive and reflexive figurative extension of deterioration and destruction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To beget evil offspring.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form IV use reported in Classical Arabic.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Corruptness or disorder in the body, intellect, or course of conduct.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal description of corruption, including bodily and intellectual disorder and corrupt conduct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Weariness, physical wasting, or debility; an extremely aged and weak person or a thing that is withering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical range of the debility branch beyond the specific Quranic state of approaching death.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person possessing no good: base, mean, sordid, bad, corrupt, neglected, or forsaken; one whose good is not hoped for and whose evil is not feared.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied as a characterization of a person and of low moral or social standing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A weak or ineffective person who does not take up arms or fight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can refer collectively to weak men who will not fight or who have no effective fighting capacity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, lean or emaciated; also vile or perishing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence specifically records applications to she-camels and, for the perishing sense, to a male camel as well.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bad or perishing language or speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative nominal use applied to language or speech.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Gypsum.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate nominal plant/mineral vocabulary use, distinct from the alkali-plant sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who burns حُرْض or other alkali plants to obtain potash; also one who fires hard stone to prepare quicklime or gypsum.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An occupational noun for processing alkali plants or stone by fire.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where alkali plants are burned to make potash, or where quicklime or gypsum is prepared by fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place noun covering the two recorded firing and preparation activities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Safflower, عُصْفُر; also its grain or safflower used in cooked meat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plant noun with the recorded culinary and general-name applications.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vessel for حُرْض or أُشْنَان, made of wood, brass, or similar material.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized container noun; its plural is مَحَارِضٌ.

cautions: حَرَضٌ in Yusuf 12:85 has a reported variant reading interpreted as حُرْضٌ, the alkali plant; the standard QAC occurrence is represented separately in the debility sense.
The QAC Form II entries are imperative surface forms; the public headword is normalized to the Classical Arabic perfect citation form حَرَّضَ.
